about: Docker tools PhageAgent MCP recommends for analysis on the user's own machine. Tools come from tool_box/bio_tools/tools_config.json (the images PhageAgent runs itself); `packages` adds images that exist only for local use (same shape as a tools_config.json entry), `overrides` changes fields of a tool for local use, `workflows` are ready-made plans.

database.note: The download creates a checkv-db-v* folder; mount that folder (the version may differ).
The iPHoP database is very large; check free disk space and https://bitbucket.org/srouxjgi/iphop first.

database.size: ~71 GB full, a few GB light
database.note: --type full creates db/ instead of db-light/ and gives better annotation.
Download the GTDB-Tk R220 reference package (https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/installing/) and unpack it into this folder.

phage_discovery.title: Find phage contigs and check their quality
phage_discovery.input: Assembled contigs or a genome, nucleotide FASTA (e.g. contigs.fna)
follow_up: Look up close relatives of the phage contigs with similarity_search on their proteins.
Compare hosts and lifestyles with search_phages / cohort_report.

phage_quality.title: Completeness and contamination of phage genomes
phage_quality.input: Phage genomes or viral contigs, nucleotide FASTA

phage_gene_annotation.title: Predict genes and match them to PhageScope
follow_up: Send up to 50 proteins from genes.faa to similarity_search to find PhageScope homologs, then search_families / get_structures for function and structure.

phage_host_prediction.title: Predict phage hosts
follow_up: Without the iPHoP database, submit_analysis can run host prediction on PhageAgent instead.

illumina_virome.title: Viromes from paired-end Illumina reads
illumina_virome.input: Paired-end reads, two FASTQ files given as r1 and r2
